messages:
Alex: Customer AcmeCorp reporting large number of failed requests from their batch job, getting HTTP 429 "rate limited" responses even though Console shows quota left for the org. Posted sample curl + response below. Need a quick unblock.

Alex: ```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer SK_ACME_***" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"input": "test"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{"error": {"message": "rate limit exceeded", "code": 429, "request_id": "req_0a1b2c3d"}}
```

Alex: Customer org_id: org_acme_42, timeframe: 2026-03-17T15:05Z -> 15:25Z.

Maria: @Devin can you grab the request_id (req_0a1b2c3d) and check enforcement logs + quota-store for org_acme_42? Also any recent rollout that touched quota-writer?

sre-bot: Alert: downstream-metering-consumer lag > 90s for partition 12 (consumer: metering-processor).

Devin: grabbing logs now. Quick findings: gateway enforcement shows many throttle decisions for org_acme_42 around 15:12Z with policy_id=rate_default. But quota-store (hot cache) returns tokens_remaining=1_234_567 at 15:11Z. That doesn't line up. Suspect write/replication lag or a write-path bug.

Maria: run this query against metrics-store and quota-writes to get last write times: ```
-- rough SQL
SELECT org_id, max(ts) as last_write, count(*) FROM quota_write_events WHERE org_id = 'org_acme_42' GROUP BY org_id;
```

Alex: Pasted results from metrics backend: ```
org_id | last_write
org_acme_42 | 2026-03-17T14:59:05Z
```

Alex: So last_write is ~16 minutes before the incidents. Console shows recent consumption because UI caches from a different view.

Devin: I pulled the full enforcement log for req_0a1b2c3d: ```
[2026-03-17T15:12:09Z] gateway enforcement decision: throttle=true org=org_acme_42 policy=rate_default reason=quota_not_found lookup_id=req_0a1b2c3d
```

Devin: I also grep'd quota-writer logs and found a stack trace around 14:58Z in the async write path. There's a new commit (7f8c2b) from earlier today that changed header parsing for token types. Repro: writes from requests using Authorization: Bearer were routed to an experimental queue and a filter dropped records if Authorization header used legacy prefix.

Maria: That sounds like a regression in the async writer that can leave the quota-store stale while UI reads a cached value from the snapshot service. Can we hotfix the writer ASAP?

Devin: Opening a hotfix PR to revert the header routing change. For immediate mitigation I can flip enforcement to soft-fail (allow) for org_acme_42 only while we validate. Will require a short deploy. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Alex: Customer is asking for a short unblock; they can throttle job if we let some requests through. Please do the soft-fail and confirm post-change.

Devin: ```PR: https://git.internal/redwood/quota-writer/pulls/2345
Action: revert commit 7f8c2b in branch hotfix/disable-experimental-token-route
Deploy: canary -> p-svc-1 (10%) -> full if green.```

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for service=quota-writer env=prod region=us-east-1 cohort=p-svc-1. Build: 1723-hotfix-2345.

sre-bot: Canary healthcheck: 200 OK for quota-write calls, consumer lag reduced to < 10s.

Devin: Canary looks good. Rolling to 100% over next 5m. Also enabled temporary soft-enforcement for org_acme_42 (id = org_acme_42) at the gateway side to avoid further customer impact.

deploy-bot: Rollout complete for quota-writer. Version 1723-hotfix-2345 -> 100% prod.

Devin: Verified quota-write events show up after the deploy; last_write now 2026-03-17T15:18:42Z. Enforcement decisions now return allow for previously-throttled requests.

Alex: Confirmed with customer, their job resumed and error rate dropped to zero. Customer appreciated the quick fix. :thumbsup:

Maria: Follow-ups: 1) postmortem for writer change and stronger pre-release checks for header routing, 2) add monitoring alert for mismatch between gateway enforcement cache and quota-store write recency, 3) update console docs to clarify which data source the UI uses (snapshot vs live write).

Devin: I'll file the postmortem and the alert. Filing now.

Alex: Thanks everyone. I'll update the ticket and close the support escalation once postmortem link is attached.
